extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, CJR‑X participant organizations, providers/suppliers, compliance officers, and stakeholders commenting on the proposed CJR‑X rule
extracted.subtask_short: CJR‑X model waivers and billing rules
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed regulatory guidance for the CJR‑X Medicare episode-based model covering enforcement, fraud/abuse waiver authority and safe harbors, documentation and retrieval requirements for beneficiary incentives, post‑discharge home visit rules (clinical, supervision, billing, limits), and telehealth waivers, coding, and payment policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation requirement for beneficiary engagement incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X participants must retain and provide access to required documentation for beneficiary engagement incentives under §512.685(d) and must retain documentation in accordance with §512.135.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documented, diligent, good faith attempts to retrieve misappropriated items of technology (if, for example, an item were sold) will be deemed to meet the retrieval requirement. CMS specifically solicits comment on the proposed documentation requirements for beneficiary engagement incentives at §512.685(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement authority not limited by model provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: OIG authority to audit, evaluate, investigate, or inspect CJR‑X participants, collaborators, agents, downstream agents, or any other persons/entities and their records/data is not limited or restricted by CJR‑X model provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No model provision limits other Government Agencies from conducting similar oversight. The proposed enforcement authority for CJR‑X would be in accordance with the standard Innovation Center model provisions at §512.160.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraud and abuse waiver authority (scope and application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 1115A(d)(1) of the Act the Secretary may waive certain statutory requirements (Titles XI and XVIII, selected sections of Medicaid/Medicare statutes) solely for purposes of testing models under section 1115A(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any waivers would apply solely to CJR‑X (and could differ from waivers for other models). No waivers are issued in the proposed rule; waivers, if any, would be in separate documentation. Absent an explicit waiver issued for CJR‑X, participants, collaborators, and agents must comply with all applicable laws and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of anti‑kickback statute safe harbor for CMS‑sponsored model arrangements and patient incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes to determine that the anti‑kickback statute safe harbor for CMS‑sponsored model arrangements and model patient incentives (42 CFR 1001.952(ii)(1) and (ii)(2)) will be available to protect certain CJR‑X remuneration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The safe harbor protection is proposed for: the sharing arrangement's gainsharing and alignment payments (if they meet safe harbor requirements and proposed §512.670), distribution arrangement payments (proposed §512.675), downstream distribution payments (proposed §512.680), and beneficiary incentives (proposed §512.685). All safe harbor requirements in 42 CFR 1001.952(ii) and the corresponding proposed §§ must be met to qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver authority to provide program flexibilities tied to episode accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS may waive Medicare program rules under section 1115A to provide flexibilities intended to increase episode quality and decrease episode spending/internal costs when CJR‑X participants bear financial responsibility for episodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waivers are intended to enable more efficient care (e.g., easing 3‑Day SNF Rule, telehealth) while maintaining quality. Waivers would apply to services furnished to CJR‑X beneficiaries who are in episodes at the time the waiver-authorized service is furnished. If a service was billed and paid only because of a CJR‑X waiver but the beneficiary was not in CJR‑X at the time of furnishing, CMS would recover payment from the provider/supplier and require repayment of beneficiary coinsurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑discharge home visits allowed (scope and clinical intent)
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X proposes to permit targeted post‑discharge in‑home visits by qualified/licensed clinicians during the episode to support follow‑up care, identify complications, reinforce discharge instructions, reconcile medications, and facilitate rehabilitation adherence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitting home visits aims to promote safe discharge to home, reduce reliance on higher‑cost institutional PAC, and potentially lower episode spending while improving quality. CMS anticipates these visits can increase patient‑centered coordination and reduce avoidable ED visits/readmissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and limits for post‑discharge home visit billing
rubrics_metrics.description: Post‑discharge home visit waiver applies only to CJR‑X beneficiaries who do NOT qualify for Medicare home health services; such visits would be unbillable for beneficiaries who qualify for home health under §409.42.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CJR‑X proposes up to 9 post‑discharge home visits billable and payable during each 90‑day post‑anchor hospitalization/anchor procedure (mirroring original CJR). The 9‑visit limit approximates weekly visits for two‑thirds of a 90‑day episode. CMS will monitor utilization and re‑evaluate necessity of the waiver over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident‑to rule waiver conditions for home visits
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X proposes waiving the Medicare 'incident to' rule (§410.26(b)(5)) to allow licensed clinical staff to furnish post‑discharge home visits under the 'general supervision' (§410.32(b)(3)(i)) of a physician or other practitioner when consistent with law, regulation, and facility policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the waiver, services may be furnished by licensed clinical staff but billed by the physician/nonphysician practitioner or by the hospital to which the supervising physician has reassigned billing rights, using a CMS‑created HCPCS G‑code specific to CJR‑X. The waiver does not apply to beneficiaries who qualify for home health services. CMS will monitor for overutilization or reductions in medically necessary care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home visit HCPCS G‑code: creation, use, and payment
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes a CJR‑X‑specific HCPCS G‑code for post‑discharge home visits to allow billing for assessment performed by clinical staff for individuals not considered homebound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The G‑code use: assessment of clinical status, safety/fall prevention, functional status/ambulation, medication reconciliation/management, compliance with plan of care, activities of daily living, connections to community services; cannot be billed for a 30‑day period covered by transitional care management code. Proposed payment ~ $50 under the physician fee schedule, with values updated annually to correspond to final PFS values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of global surgical billing for post‑discharge home visits
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes to waive current global surgery billing rules to allow separate reporting and billing for CJR‑X post‑discharge home visits during surgical global periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS believes the CJR‑X home visits complement rather than duplicate typical post‑operative global care; the waiver permits these visits to be billed separately by the surgeon or other practitioners during the global period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telehealth geographic and originating site waivers for CJR‑X beneficiaries
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X proposes waiving the telehealth geographic site requirements (section 1834(m)(4)(C)(i)(I)–(III)) and originating site requirements (section 1834(m)(4)(C)(ii)(I)–(X)) to allow telehealth services furnished to CJR‑X beneficiaries at their home/place of residence during the episode regardless of geography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver of geographic site allows beneficiaries in any region to receive episode‑related telehealth services (so long as other Medicare telehealth payment requirements are met). Waiver of originating site is limited to telehealth services furnished in the beneficiary's home during the episode. Services must be on the Medicare list of telehealth services and meet all other Medicare telehealth payment requirements; some services whose descriptors preclude home delivery still cannot be furnished in the home (e.g., subsequent hospital care when patient is not an inpatient).

rubrics_metrics.name: Telehealth services exclusion/episode definition linkage
rubrics_metrics.description: Only services on the Medicare approved telehealth services list that are not excluded from the proposed episode definition may be furnished to CJR‑X beneficiaries via the CJR‑X telehealth waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS refers commenters to the proposed episode definition (section X.C.2.d.(3).) for exclusions. Even if eligible under the waiver, HCPCS code descriptors that preclude home delivery take precedence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation of home E/M telehealth HCPCS G‑codes and coding structure
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes creating four HCPCS G‑codes to describe E/M services furnished to CJR‑X beneficiaries in their homes via telehealth, structured parallel to office/outpatient E/M CPT codes (especially CPT 99212–99215 for established patient visits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The codes will reflect the beneficiary's residence as location and virtual presence of the practitioner. Example: a level 3 established patient G‑code would require at least 2 of 3 key components (expanded problem‑focused history, expanded problem‑focused exam, medical decision making of low complexity), and typical time expectations (e.g., ~20 minutes via audio/video). CMS will publish precise G‑codes prior to PY1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment rates and RVU policy for telehealth home E/M G‑codes
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes to set payment rates for the new telehealth home E/M G‑codes similar to the office/outpatient E/M services, adopting corresponding work and malpractice (MP) RVUs under the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resource costs included should reflect professional time, intensity, and malpractice risk. CMS expects to include final RVUs under the CY 2027 PFS for PY1 and update annually to match PFS final values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice expense (PE) RVU policy for telehealth home E/M G‑codes
rubrics_metrics.description: For lower level telehealth home E/M visits (levels 2 and 3 established visits), CMS proposes not to include PE RVUs because virtual visits generally do not incur the kinds of practice expense costs captured in PE RVUs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For higher level visits (levels 4 and 5) CMS anticipates auxiliary licensed clinical staff support is typical, but does not propose to incorporate those costs via PE RVUs. CMS expects that level 4/5 telehealth home visits will often be reported with a same‑date home visit or during authorized home health care; if not, physicians must document auxiliary staff availability or explain why such staff were not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auxiliary licensed clinical staff expectations and documentation for high‑level telehealth visits
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS expects that level 4 or 5 E/M telehealth home visits will typically require auxiliary licensed clinical staff to be present in the patient's home for complete service delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a level 4/5 telehealth home visit is billed without an accompanying in‑home visit or home health period, the physician must document in the medical record that auxiliary licensed clinical staff were available on site during the visit; if they were not present, document the reason why such personnel were not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction of CJR‑X telehealth rules with home health services and certification face‑to‑face requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Telehealth visits under CJR‑X cannot substitute for in‑person home health visits (section 1895(e)(1)(A)) and telehealth by social workers cannot be furnished to beneficiaries in a home health episode because medical social services are included in HH PPS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physicians and allowed NPPs (PAs, NPs, CNSs, CNMs, CRNAs, psychologists, dieticians) can furnish telehealth while beneficiaries are in a home health episode and be paid under section 1834 of the Act, subject to usual rules. However, the face‑to‑face encounter required for home health certification (sections 1835(a), 1814(a), and §424.22) is not covered by the CJR‑X waiver when furnished via telehealth; usual telehealth geography/originating site rules apply to that encounter.

rubrics_metrics.name: No additional telehealth payment for technology/setup and facility fee waiver when home is originating site
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the proposed CJR‑X telehealth waivers, no additional payment would be made to cover set‑up costs, technology purchases, training/education, or other related costs. The facility fee for an originating site would be waived if there is no facility (i.e., the service originated in the beneficiary's home).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers/suppliers furnishing telehealth to a CJR‑X beneficiary in the home may not bill for telehealth services that were not fully furnished due to technical issues with telecommunications equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and reassessment of waiver utilization and integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS will monitor utilization patterns for waivers (e.g., incident‑to home visit waiver, telehealth use) to detect overutilization or reductions in medically necessary care and will reassess waiver necessity if utilization indicates limited benefit or misuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS notes prior low utilization in some models (e.g., TEAM) informed decisions to continue waivers for continuity; ongoing monitoring may prompt future modifications or rescission of waivers.
